FINITE EQUILIBRIUM CALCULATOR

A spherical, pressure-supported halo

Numerically integrated · King family

Explore a known lowered-isothermal equilibrium with a finite zero-density edge. This baseline has no baryonic disk, rotation-curve fitting or inferred viscosity.

M☉ / kpc³ · logarithmic control

Finite edge—
Total halo mass—
Scale radius r₀—

Density and pressure vanish at the finite edge. Outside it, the gravitational field has a Keplerian circular-speed tail.

∂

Equilibrium is a testable model, not a detection of a fluid. The solver integrates dW/dx = −m/x² and dm/dx = x²ρ/ρ₀. The velocity scale s is not a constant local dispersion: pressure comes from the lowered distribution's own velocity moment. A matching rotation curve would not establish dark-matter microphysics or image-based distance.

AP = average precision within a fixed angular annulus. Unmarked regions are incomplete labels. Low-vote objects had no spatial arm task and supply no negative truth.

DISTANCE QUESTION

Better arm maps did not establish better redshifts.

For the 59 fresh strong-spiral galaxies, mean absolute catalog-redshift error was 0.01277 using photometry, size and basic image features, and 0.01253 after adding arm scores.

Equal sky-group improvement · 95% interval+0.00044 [−0.00055, +0.00144]

The interval includes zero. This selected same-survey cohort does not establish an incremental distance benefit. Catalog redshift prediction also differs from an independent geometric distance measurement.

i

Failures stay in the denominator. One of 99 images failed input guards. Its identity and unchanged catalog predictions remain in the redshift evaluation. AP is undefined for absent or one-class spatial annotations. These results do not validate automatic arm centerlines, pitch, physical widths or viscosity.
